dataset: Sourced energy-code and mechanical-code requirements for insulating HVAC ductwork by duct type (supply, return, outdoor-air intake incl. combustion/makeup air, exhaust, relief, transfer) and duct location (conditioned, unconditioned incl. attic/crawl space/garage, indirectly conditioned incl. return plenums, semiheated, outdoors, buried/underground, within the building envelope assembly), with verbatim definitions, exceptions, residential rules, condensation/vapor clauses, the DOE 2012 code-note duct-location key, and notes on conflicts. Companion to code-requirements-verified.json (DUCT-1..DUCT-16), which is cited, not repeated.

conventions.unverified: The literal string 'unverified' (or an entry in the top-level 'unverified' list) means no fetched source stated the item. Nothing was guessed, interpolated or filled from memory.
conventions.src: Every item carries 'src', a list of source ids. 'D_C1'...'D_C27' are records in this file's 'sources' array. Plain 'C1'...'C35' ids are the source records of code-requirements-verified.json (same documents re-read for this file); their titles are repeated in 'reused_source_ids' below. D_C19, D_C20 and D_C26 document searches or files that yielded no requirement text.

reused_source_ids.C1: IECC 2021 Chapter 4 [CE] (UpCodes, Colorado, Adopts Without Amendments)
reused_source_ids.C19: ASHRAE addenda be...cy to 90.1-2016 consolidated reprint (treated as 90.1-2019 text)
reused_source_ids.C21: ASHRAE Standards Addenda index + bulk search of 195 90.1 addenda PDFs
reused_source_ids.C22: NYC Energy Code 2025 6.8.2 Duct Insulation Tables (UpCodes snippet)
reused_source_ids.C23: NYC Energy Code 2025 Chapter 6 (90.1-2022 as amended by NYC)

conventions.cross_refs: 'see' fields such as 'DUCT-1' or 'DUCT-15' point to requirement ids in code-requirements-verified.json; 'DM-n' are cells of this file's requirements_matrix, 'EX-n' exceptions, 'RES-n' residential rows, 'CV-n' condensation/vapor items, 'DEF-n' definitions, 'DL-n' DOE duct-location items.
conventions.quotes: 'quote', '*_quote(s)', 'definition' and 'check*' strings are verbatim from the fetched page text or pdftotext output with line breaks joined and runs of spaces collapsed; for PDFs, words split by a line-end hyphen were rejoined (e.g. 'sys- tem' -> 'system'). Every such string was machine-checked as a substring of the downloaded source text when this file was built (whitespace-collapsed; for PDFs also hyphenation-insensitive). Strings read from a rendered page image instead of the text layer are in fields ending '_image_read'.
conventions.upcodes_formatting: UpCodes text loses superscripts: 'ft2' means ft^2, 'R-valuea,b' means R-value with footnotes a,b; ' | ' separates table cells.
conventions.icc_via_state_adoptions: ICC model codes (IECC, IMC, IRC) were read from UpCodes pages of state adoptions whose header says 'Adopts Without Amendments'; the edition shown is the model edition named on that page.
conventions.state_amendments: Washington (D_C21) and Minnesota (D_C22, D_C23) are STATE amendments, not model code. They are included only because they are the sources found that assign R-values to outdoor-air, exhaust and relief ducts; never apply them outside those states.

status_values.stated: the code text itself states the requirement for this duct type and location
status_values.none_stated: the code text explicitly says no insulation (e.g. 'None', 'do not require insulation', an exception)
status_values.not_addressed: the code's duct-insulation clause is limited to other duct types or locations, so it sets no R-value here (other clauses such as IMC 603.12 condensation control may still apply)
status_values.derived: the requirement follows from combining quoted definitions with quoted requirement text; this is the agent's reading and is flagged so a user can override it
status_values.partially_verified: values verified for some climate zones only
status_values.unverified: not found in any fetched source

conventions.summaries: Fields named 'note', 'reading', 'parsed', 'difference' or 'summary' are the agent's paraphrase or structured reading of the quotes; the quotes govern.

units.R: h·ft²·°F/Btu, installed (see code-requirements-verified.json DUCT-9..DUCT-12 for installed-thickness rules)

conventions.climate_zones: ASHRAE 90.1/IECC zones 0-8 unless noted. California Title 24 uses California climate zones 1-16. Washington tables list only zones 4C and 5B.

items.definition: space: an enclosed space within a building. The classifications of spaces are as follows for the purpose of determining building envelope requirements: conditioned space: a cooled space, heated space, or indirectly conditioned space defined as follows:
sub_definitions: a. cooled space: an enclosed space within a building that is cooled by a cooling system whose sensible output capacity is
heated space: an enclosed space within a building that is heated by a heating system whose output capacity relative to the floor area is greater than or equal to the criteria in Table 3.2.
items.glyph_note: In C19 the comparison sign before '3.4 Btu/h·ft2 of floor area' in 'cooled space' is a missing glyph in both the text layer and the rendered page (PDF p. 24, read at 100 dpi); the 90.1-2022 text (DEF-2) and the D_C16 package print '≥3.4'.
items.note: 90.1 counts indirectly conditioned space as conditioned space by definition, yet Table 6.8.2 has a separate 'Indirectly Conditioned Space' column and Exception 2 to 6.4.4.1.2 exempts only heated, semiheated and cooled spaces (see notes, N-1).

items.definition: cooled space: an enclosed space within a building that is cooled by a cooling system whose sensible output capacity is ≥3.4 Btu/h•ft2 of floor area.
also_quotes: conditioned space: a cooled space, heated space, or indirectly conditioned space defined as follows:
heated space: an enclosed space within a building that is heated by a heating system whose output capacity relative to the floor area is greater than or equal to the criteria in Table 3.2.

cross_check.quote: capacity is ≥3.4 Btu/h·ft2 of floor floor area.
cross_check.note: ASHRAE Addendum r to 90.1-2022 shows the national 2022 'cooled space' text with 'floor' struck and re-inserted as a defined term (pdftotext prints both).

items.definition: An area, room or space that is enclosed within the building thermal envelope and is directly or indirectly heated or cooled. Spaces are indirectly heated or cooled where they communicate through openings with conditioned spaces, where they are separated from conditioned spaces by uninsulated walls, floors or ceilings, or where they contain uninsulated ducts, piping or other sources of heating or cooling.

An area, room or space that is enclosed within the building thermal envelope and is directly or indirectly heated or cooled. Spaces are indirectly heated or cooled where they communicate through openings with conditioned spaces, where they are separated from conditioned spaces by uninsulated walls, floors or ceilings, or where they contain uninsulated ducts, piping or other sources of heating or cooling.

An area, room or space that is enclosed within the building thermal envelope and that is directly or indirectly heated or cooled. Spaces are indirectly heated or cooled where they communicate through openings with conditioned spaces, where they are separated from conditioned spaces by uninsulated walls, floors or ceilings, or where they contain uninsulated ducts, piping or other sources of heating or cooling.

An area, room or space that is enclosed within the building thermal envelope and that is directly heated or cooled or that is indirectly heated or cooled. Spaces are indirectly heated or cooled where they communicate through openings with conditioned spaces, where they are separated from conditioned spaces by uninsulated walls, floors or ceilings, or where they contain uninsulated ducts, piping or other sources of heating or cooling.
CONDITIONED SPACE is an enclosed space within a building that is directly conditioned or indirectly conditioned.
also_quotes: CONDITIONED SPACE, DIRECTLY is an enclosed space that is provided with wood heating, mechanical heating that has a capacity exceeding 10 Btu/hr-ft², or mechanical cooling that has a capacity exceeding 5 Btu/hr-ft², .

items.definition: indirectly conditioned space: an enclosed space within a building that is not a heated space or a cooled space, which is heated or cooled indirectly by being connected to adjacent spaces, provided:
conditions: the product of the U-factors and surface areas of the space adjacent to connected spaces exceeds the combined sum of the product of the U-factors and surface areas of the space adjoining the outdoors, unconditioned spaces, and to or from semiheated spaces (e.g., corridors) or
that air from heated or cooled spaces is intentionally transferred (naturally or mechanically) into the space at a rate exceeding 3 ach (e.g., atria).

table_link.quote: Includes return air plenums with or without exposed roofs above.
table_link.note: Table 6.8.2 footnote c on the 'Indirectly Conditioned Space' column (DUCT-1).

items.definition: indirectly conditioned space: an enclosed space within a building that is not a heated space or a cooled space, which is heated or cooled indirectly by being connected to adjacent spaces, provided
conditions: the product of the U-factors and surface areas of the space adjacent to connected spaces exceeds the combined sum of the product of the U-factors and surface areas of the space adjoining the outdoors, unconditioned spaces, and to or from semiheated spaces (e.g., corridors) or
that air from heated or cooled spaces is intentionally transferred (naturally or mechanically) into the space at a rate exceeding 3 ach (e.g., atria).

items.definition: CONDITIONED SPACE, INDIRECTLY is enclosed space that (1) is not directly conditioned space; and (2) either (a) has a thermal transmittance area product (UA) to directly conditioned space exceeding that to the outdoors or to unconditioned space and does not have fixed vents or openings to the outdoors or to unconditioned space, or (b) is a space through which air from directly conditioned spaces is transferred at a rate exceeding three air changes per hour.

Spaces are indirectly heated or cooled where they communicate through openings with conditioned spaces, where they are separated from conditioned spaces by uninsulated walls, floors or ceilings, or where they contain uninsulated ducts, piping or other sources of heating or cooling.
items.note: The ICC codes have no 'indirectly conditioned space' term; indirectly heated or cooled spaces are part of 'Conditioned Space' (DEF-3..DEF-6).

items.definition: semiheated space: an enclosed space within a building that is heated by a heating system whose output capacity is greater than or equal to 3.4 Btu/h·ft2 of floor area but is not a conditioned space.
semiheated space: an enclosed space within a building that is heated by a heating system whose output capacity is greater than or equal to 3.4 Btu/h•ft2 of floor area but is not a conditioned space.
items.note: No 'semiheated space' definition was found in IECC 2021/2024 Chapter 2 (CE or RE), IMC 2021/2024 Chapter 2 or the Title 24 2022 definitions searched.

items.definition: unconditioned space: an enclosed space within a building that is not a conditioned space or a semiheated space. Crawlspaces, attics, and parking garages with natural or mechanical ventilation are not considered enclosed spaces.

unconditioned space: an enclosed space within a building that is not a conditioned space or a semi-heated space. Crawlspaces, attics, and parking garages with natural or mechanical ventilation are not considered enclosed spaces.

items.definition: building envelope: the exterior plus the semiexterior portions of a building. For the purposes of determining building envelope requirements, the classifications are defined as follows: exterior building envelope: the elements of a building that separate conditioned spaces from the exterior. semiexterior building envelope: the elements of a building that separate conditioned space from unconditioned space or that enclose semiheated spaces through which thermal energy may be transferred to or from the exterior, to or from unconditioned spaces, or to or from conditioned spaces.

items.definition: That air delivered to each or any space supplied by the air distribution system or the total air delivered to all spaces supplied by the air distribution system, which is provided for ventilating, heating, cooling, humidification, dehumidification and other similar purposes.
also_quotes: An assembly of connected ducts, plenums, fittings, registers and grilles through which air, heated or cooled, is conducted from the supply unit to the space or spaces to be heated or cooled

items.definition: AIR, SUPPLY is air entering a space from an air-conditioning, heating, or ventilating system for the purpose of comfort conditioning. Supply air is generally filtered, fan-forced, and heated, cooled, humidified or dehumidified as necessary to maintain specified temperature and humidity conditions.

The assemblies of connected ducts, plenums, boots, fittings, dampers, supply registers, return grilles, and filter grilles through which air is supplied to or returned from the space to be heated, cooled, or ventilated. Supply ductwork delivers air to the spaces from the space conditioning equipment. Return ductwork conveys air from the spaces back to the space conditioning equipment. Ventilation ductwork conveys air to or from any space.
Air removed from an approved conditioned space or location and recirculated or exhausted.
also_quotes: An assembly of connected ducts, plenums, fittings, registers and grilles through which air from the space or spaces to be heated or cooled is conducted back to the supply unit

items.definition: Ambient air that enters a building through a ventilation system, through intentional openings for natural ventilation, or by infiltration.
also_quotes: Air taken from the outdoors, and therefore not previously circulated through the system.
items.note: The IMC defines the term twice ('Air, Outdoor' and 'Outdoor Air'); both are quoted.

items.definition: outdoor (outside) air: air that is outside the building envelope or is taken from outside the building that has not been previously circulated through the building.
OUTDOOR AIR (Outside air) is air taken from outdoors and not previously circulated in the building.
That portion of supply air that comes from outside (outdoors) plus any recirculated air that has been treated to maintain the desired quality of air within a designated space.
also_quotes: The natural or mechanical process of supplying conditioned or unconditioned air to, or removing such air from, any space.

items.definition: Any combination of outdoor and transfer air intended to replace exhaust air and exfiltration.

makeup air (dedicated replacement air): outdoor air deliberately brought into the building from the outside and supplied to the vicinity of an exhaust hood to replace air, vapor, and contaminants being exhausted. Makeup air is generally filtered and fan-forced, and it may be heated or cooled depending on the requirements of the application. Makeup air may be delivered through outlets integral to the exhaust hood or through outlets in the same room.

items.term_as_printed: Air, Exhaust; Exhaust System; Environmental Air

notes.note: Attic, crawl space and parking garage conflict: 90.1-2019 puts 'attics above insulated ceilings, parking garages and crawl spaces' in the Exterior column (H&C R-8 CZ 0-4, R-12 CZ 5-8), while IECC 2021/2024 commercial names only 'unconditioned spaces' (R-6) and 'outside the building' (R-8/R-12). Treating these spaces as IECC 'unconditioned' (DOE's 2012 reading of the same wording) gives R-6 where 90.1 gives R-12 in CZ 5-8. The simulator should show both and label the IECC value 'derived'.

Service type matters only under ASHRAE 90.1: Table 6.8.2 has separate rows for heating-and-cooling, heating-only and cooling-only ducts (e.g. cooling-only CZ 7-8 is R-1.9 in every location; heating-only CZ 0-1 is None). IECC, Title 24 and IECC residential do not split by service.

Outdoor-air intake, exhaust, relief and transfer ducts: none of ASHRAE 90.1-2019/2022, IECC 2021/2024 (commercial C403.12.1/C403.13.1, residential R403.3) or Title 24 2022 120.4 assigns them an R-value; the DOE 2012 code note says so explicitly for exhaust. What does apply: IMC 603.12 (prevent exterior condensation on any duct), IMC 604.2 (120°F surface limit), ASHRAE 62.1 5.14.2 (insulate surfaces below the surrounding dew point), and the IECC combustion-air duct rule (R-8 through conditioned space, CZ 3-8). For these duct types a simulator should report 'no code-minimum R (not addressed)' and size insulation by condensation/heat-gain calculation, unless a state amendment (Washington, Minnesota) is selected.

Shutoff dampers vs insulation: 90.1 6.4.3.4.2 and IECC C403.7.7 require motorized (or, in listed cases, gravity) dampers on outdoor-air intake and exhaust openings, but neither ties duct insulation to the damper position. The 'insulate from the building exterior to the automatic shutoff damper' concept was found only in Washington C403.10.1.1 (state) and in the intent statement of Canada's NECB 2011 Sentence 5.2.4.2.(3) ('ducts located between dampers and the building envelope'); it was not found in any ASHRAE 90.1 or IECC text read.

Runout exception (90.1 Exception 3) is a cap ('need not exceed R-3.5'), not an exemption; it does not reduce the R-1.9 required for supply runouts in return plenums.
